title: 差价好几千，苹果官翻机爆发，「官换机」趁机套路消费者？
content: Apple's Mac price hikes—blamed on rising storage costs—have made official refurbished Macs more attractive. These "Apple Certified Refurbished" products now offer meaningful savings since third-party discounts have shrunk. They undergo full refurbishment with new batteries and casings, include standard warranties, and are increasingly available with newer models. Meanwhile, "official replacement" machines sold by third parties carry major risks: unclear provenance, shortened warranties, and potential use of non-original parts. Across the PC industry, Windows manufacturers have operated refurbished programs for years. As hardware costs rise globally, certified refurbs are becoming a practical alternative for budget-conscious buyers.

title: Cursor，即将彻底消失？
content: SpaceX is acquiring Cursor for $60 billion, with the deal expected to close by late August. The Cursor brand will be phased out from new products; its unreleased AI agent "Sand" will likely launch as "Grok Bot." Cursor will not operate as an independent entity—its teams will be absorbed into SpaceXAI. Existing Cursor tools will temporarily keep their name. The acquisition gives SpaceXAI access to Cursor's 50,000 enterprise clients, over one million paid users, and extensive coding data, addressing its weakness in enterprise coding tools where competitors like Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex lead.

title: 谷歌AI，杯酒释兵权
content:
Google reorganized its AI leadership on August 6 without public conflict. DeepMind founder Demis Hassabis became Alphabet's chief scientist for long-term AGI strategy, while veteran engineer Koray Kavukcuoglu took operational control of Gemini. Jeff Dean, Google's chief scientist and leader of Google Brain, departed to start a company that Google promptly invested in.

The moves completed CEO Sundar Pichai's three-year consolidation of AI power. Since merging Google Brain and DeepMind in 2023, Pichai has systematically transferred control from academic founders to operational managers, eliminating the decade-long internal rivalry between research and engineering cultures while maintaining relationships through strategic titles and investments.

content: OpenAI is voluntarily slowing development of its next-generation model Astra due to cybersecurity risks. Internal assessments found the model could write code, find vulnerabilities, plan attacks, and execute tasks autonomously—capabilities approaching a skilled hacker. The company is implementing isolated testing environments and universal monitoring while delaying release until enhanced safety measures are complete. CEO Sam Altman confirmed the decision, citing OpenAI's 2023 Preparedness Framework. OpenAI voluntarily informed the U.S. government, marking a rare instance of a frontier AI lab deliberately decelerating core research over safety concerns rather than competitive pressure.

content: High intelligence often hinders online success because smart people overcomplicate simple methods, let ego trap them in credentials, and seek permission rather than taking action. The internet rewards daily execution, simplicity, and courage—not degrees, complex plans, or sophistication. Online business requires one platform, one product, one funnel, and relentless consistency. Success comes from helping others genuinely, building simple systems, tracking daily metrics, and being authentic. The author draws from personal experience rejecting a high-profile job, banking career, and coaching 6,000+ people to conclude: action beats intelligence, and complexity prevents profits.

title: Keeping ChatGPT Fast as AI Development Accelerates
content: Martin Spier, who leads ChatGPT Performance at OpenAI, discusses how agentic workflows have dramatically increased code shipping velocity. As user growth accelerates globally and development becomes more parallel through AI agents, traditional performance engineering cannot keep pace manually. He emphasizes that AI performance involves far more than GPUs—data fetching, tokenization, serialization, and network requests all contribute significantly to latency. Spier advocates for always-on AI agents that automate profiling, regression detection, and continuous optimization across both reactive troubleshooting and proactive improvement loops. Success requires strong engineering fundamentals: comprehensive testing, benchmarks, observability, and safe deployment practices to enable agents to complete full optimization autonomously.
